prompts.text: Which family photograph makes everyone tell a different version of what happened?
Describe a time you recognised a relative in an old photograph only from their smile.
Recreate a family picture in the same outfits or in the same location?
Your family must select one picture for an imaginary museum exhibit. Which would cause the longest debate?
The person taking family photos often ends up appearing in the fewest of them.
The funniest family photographs are often the ones nobody intended to take.
Whose childhood photo looks least like the person they are today?
Recall discovering a family photo with a mysterious person in the background.
Everyone is asked to bring a photo representing their most memorable family meal. What would you choose?
A family photo wall with captions or a digital album with recorded stories?
Which relative gives the most entertaining directions around town?
Tell us about a relative who knew a surprising shortcut nobody else believed in.
Follow a family elder's directions without a map or let the youngest navigate using an app?
The family has to invent nicknames for ten familiar landmarks. Which place gets the funniest name?
Families sometimes navigate by shops or trees that disappeared many years ago.
A detailed landmark is better than a confident instruction to turn somewhere nearby.
What place does your family describe with a name that no longer appears on maps?
Recall two relatives arguing about the best route and discovering both were wrong.
You must give directions to your childhood home using only memories. Which detail do you mention first?
A historical tour led by a grandparent or a present-day tour led by a cousin?
Which tiny responsibility did you pretend to take very seriously as a child?
Describe helping an elder with a task and making the task twice as long.
Let younger cousins organise the seating or let them design the menu cards?
Children take charge of a family celebration's opening announcement. What should their speech include?
Children often remember the feeling of having a role more than the result of the task.
A family job is more fun when it gives children genuine responsibility rather than just a title.
Who in your family first trusted you with a task usually reserved for adults?
Tell us about earning an elder's trust after an attempt went wrong.
Your relatives create a pretend office for running family events. Who becomes the funniest manager?
Give children a small event-planning budget or ask them to build the decorations?
Which relative would win a competition for telling the longest story before reaching the point?
Recall a family storyteller adding a dramatic detail nobody else remembered.
Hear one elder tell a complete childhood adventure or five relatives describe the same incident?
Each family member gets sixty seconds to narrate an old misunderstanding. Who would need extra time?
Family stories often come with interruptions from people correcting tiny details.
A well-told story deserves to be enjoyed even when the listener already knows the ending.
Which family story is always accompanied by somebody saying it didn't happen like that?
Describe hearing the untold ending of a story you had known since childhood.
The family appoints a historian for one evening. Which disputed event should they investigate first?
Record a lively family story session or write a collection of short memories together?
What's the most creative homemade gift you've received from a relative?
Tell us about somebody keeping a small item you made long after you forgot it.
Trade handmade bookmarks or write each other funny appreciation certificates?
Every relative must create a gift using materials already at home. What would you make?
The effort behind a homemade present often becomes part of the present's story.
A useful handmade item deserves as much appreciation as a polished store-bought one.
Which object in your home would make the most surprising family heirloom?
Describe finding a handwritten message tucked into something an elder had kept.
A family keepsake has no known owner. How should everyone decide where it belongs?
Preserve a relative's recipe book or their collection of handwritten letters?
Which everyday sound reminds you of a relative's home?
Tell us about hearing a song that immediately brought back an old family gathering.
Record the sounds of a familiar kitchen or collect songs from important family celebrations?
Each family member chooses a sound effect for their entrance at the next reunion. What would yours be?
The ordinary noises of home often become more noticeable after somebody moves away.
A house can feel familiar before you recognise anything you see.
Which family member could you recognise instantly from the sound of their footsteps?
Recall somebody calling your name in a way no one outside your family would use.
Your family's everyday routines become an audio play. What sound begins the first scene?
Listen to old voice recordings together or create a fresh family radio-style show?
What is the most amusing difference between how two relatives organise their homes?
Describe a family visit when you discovered an unexpectedly clever storage trick.
Help an organised relative label their shelves or help a creative relative redesign a room?
Two family members are asked to arrange the same living room for a party. How different would their plans be?
People who grew up in one household still develop entirely different decorating preferences.
A comfortable family home doesn't need to look like everybody else's.
Which room in a relative's home always feels inviting, and what makes it so?
Tell us about a family member who made space for a guest despite a crowded house.
Your relatives swap one harmless home-improvement suggestion each. What would you recommend?
Build a family memory corner or decorate a shared table for gatherings?
Which relative is most likely to remember a celebration that everybody else forgot?
Recall a time someone in the family rescued a plan by remembering a small detail.
Use a shared calendar for family events or have a rotating reminder captain?
Your family accidentally plans two gatherings for the same date. How should the organisers decide?
Family schedules become more complicated as people move and build new routines.
An event is easier to enjoy when people are free to explain their availability honestly.
What's the most inventive way your family has celebrated something remotely?
Tell us about joining a family occasion over the phone and still feeling involved.
A distant relative can attend for only ten minutes online. What part of the gathering should they join?
Send a group celebration video or mail one card signed by everyone?
What unusual lesson about friendship did you learn from watching relatives?
Describe witnessing two family members settle a silly disagreement in a surprising way.
Ask elders about their closest childhood friends or ask cousins how they make friends today?
Two relatives have different views on sharing personal news with the family. How could they discuss it?
Even people in one family can have very different ideas about how often to keep in touch.
Being close to a relative doesn't mean agreeing with every opinion they hold.
What kind of boundary do you respect more now than when you were younger?
Recall a relative showing support without trying to make a decision for you.
A family group chat grows too noisy for some members. What fun, fair rule could improve it?
A monthly family news roundup or occasional private one-to-one calls?
Which family member taught you to laugh at ordinary mistakes without feeling embarrassed?
Tell us about a harmless family mishap that later became a source of encouragement.
Swap stories about lessons learnt the hard way or compare the tiny victories nobody celebrated?
The family creates a cheerful awards ceremony for people who tried something new. What categories would it include?
People learn what is safe to attempt partly from how their relatives respond to mistakes.
A home feels more welcoming when imperfect attempts are treated with patience.
What could our family do to make a newcomer feel comfortable asking basic questions?
Recall a younger relative surprising everybody by trying something bold and harmless.
Every family member chooses one new skill to practise over a weekend. What would you pick?
Celebrate a first attempt with a funny certificate or gather to watch everyone demonstrate what they learnt?
